title: Readiness: what adoption arriving in a lump would need
description:
Not a schedule. A list of things that have to be TRUE before the project
is adopted at scale, each of which becomes impossible rather than merely
expensive once it is.

THE DISTINCTION THAT MAKES THIS AN EPIC. The roadmap's items 1 through 4
-- breadth of sources, X.509, Windows, enrollment -- get done because
feature work is legible: someone can see it, demo it, and take credit
for it. The items in this epic do not get done as a side effect of
working that list, because nobody gets credit for a version tag nobody
needed yet. They are also the only ones with a deadline that is not ours
to move: the first serious integrator sets it, and after that every one
of these costs a migration instead of an afternoon.

So the test for membership is not "is this important" but "does the cost
of this go from an afternoon to a migration on a date we do not
control".

WHAT PROMPTED IT. A scenario run 2026-09-16: a government mandate in
2029 requiring HIRE for workloads with a human principal, and HIRE
presence for presence-sensitive ones. The feature gaps it exposed were
all on the roadmap already and would be closed by then. The gaps it
exposed that were NOT on the roadmap are these, and a mandate is only
one of the ways adoption arrives suddenly. An acquisition, a popular
framework depending on it, or one large vendor shipping it does the
same thing.

UPSTREAM.md already contains the seed of this in its list of what
donation would cost: the trademark, unilateral direction, freedom to
change the wire format. Under sudden adoption every one of those
inverts and becomes an asset rather than a cost. That inversion is the
argument for treating this epic as P1 while nothing is forcing it.
